note: PR #70. Opened by the coordinator after the user challenged a number I had reported twice ('arch-rules 4/0 ?'). Two review rounds, both independent — the author does not approve his own work, and that rule applied to me.

events.note: The defect was in the TOOL, not only in my reporting. arch-rules printed `4 rule(s), 0 failing` for a run that was 1 proved / 3 UNKNOWN / 0 violations. The JSON had always carried `unknown` honestly; only the default TEXT output omitted it — and the omission was asymmetric in a way that hid itself: VACUOUS and NOT_COMPUTED each got an explanatory addendum, while UNKNOWN, the most common of the three and the only fail-OPEN one, got none. It survived because all 16 pre-existing tests in rules.ml assert against --format json.
events.verified: red-before-green: with the summary reverted and the test kept, the run fails on '1 proved not found' and '1 UNKNOWN not found'.

blocking: HIGH-1: `proved` was printed for rules the tool itself annotates as vacuous. Dep and Exported emitted PASS with no vacuity check, so a rule whose selector matched nothing printed `1 proved` TWO LINES BELOW a note saying the selector matched nothing. --on-vacuous fail could not catch it because only reach emits NO_SOURCE.
HIGH-2: the new parenthetical stated a policy not in force — 'fail-open by default' under --on-unknown fail — and double-counted: 1 proved + 3 failing + 1 UNKNOWN = 5 over 4 rules.
events.note: Both blockers were MY OWN defect class reappearing in the text I added to fix it. Also found: POSSIBLE was the state I forgot, fail-open and named nowhere in either channel.

refused_two_prescriptions: exported: returning NO_SOURCE on an empty selector would DOWNGRADE A VIOLATION ACTUALLY FOUND into a vacuity — with an empty selector and exports present, every export is an offender.

dep: a target-side check would FAIL THE BUILD PRECISELY WHEN THE CODEBASE IS CLEAN. A dep target ranges over module paths already depended on, so 'nothing matches Web.**' means the preventive rule is SUCCEEDING — and `forbid dep from module:lib/core/** to module:Web.**` is the tool's own documented usage example.
events.design_call: Rather than choose between §10.5's `violations` and the shipped `failing`, print BOTH on separate lines: a seven-state census that partitions the rules (checked at runtime — a verdict escaping the census aborts rather than being silently dropped), and a gate line echoing the flags actually in force. Zeros printed unconditionally, because 'a state visible only when non-zero is indistinguishable from a state the tool does not have, and 0 proved is the most important thing this line ever says.'

events.adjudication: Round 1 was WRONG ON BOTH, decisively — settled by IMPLEMENTING its prescriptions as mutants rather than by argument. N5b printed VACUOUS above the list of offenders it had just found; N4 failed the default gate on the tool's own documented example. Also verified the new vacuity verdicts are VIOLATION-PRESERVING (source_size = 0 implies hits = []), which is the question I should have asked when I relayed the prescription and did not.
events.partition_verified: 32 runs across all 16 --on-* combinations on two 9-rule fixtures: partition_ok in every one, text and JSON agreeing on every count.
findings: MEDIUM-1: SEVEN more occurrences of the misreading still in briefs/, two carrying a green check in a QA table and a ship-gate table — the exact artifact the PR exists to remove, in a PR about removing it. Round 1 named three; the sweep was partial.
MEDIUM-2: a false count ('five' for 'six') and a BROKEN MARKDOWN TABLE, both in the text this PR added.
MEDIUM-3: the --format md bullet split is load-bearing, documented as load-bearing, and untested — mutant N10 survived.
MEDIUM-4: 'the gate is UNCHANGED' is true only for reach rules; dep/exported/effect gain a fail-closed vacuity verdict that can turn a downstream green build red.

events.note: All four MEDIUMs plus both LOWs closed. The agent hit a spend limit and its LAST MESSAGE read as if it had done nothing — but it had pushed two commits and closed five of six items. An agent's final message is not the state of its work; the artifact is. I nearly relaunched the whole brief.

events.verified_before_merge: 163/163 on a clean build under a verified switch, and the actual output printed and read rather than inferred.
